reference.source: Scriver's OMMBID (Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease)
clinicalPearls: Autosomal recessive deficiency of SCOT (OXCT1 gene), the enzyme that activates acetoacetate for peripheral utilisation, is the classic pure ketolysis defect
Presents with recurrent, often severe ketoacidotic crises, characteristically beginning in the neonatal period or infancy and precipitated by fasting or infection
A hallmark is persistent ketosis even between crises and in the fed state, because ketone bodies cannot be used by peripheral tissues
Unlike beta-ketothiolase deficiency, urine organic acids show only the ketone bodies (large amounts of acetoacetate and 3-hydroxybutyrate) without the abnormal isoleucine metabolites
The acylcarnitine profile is typically normal, so the diagnosis is easily overlooked on newborn screening
Acute treatment reverses catabolism with intravenous glucose and corrects acidosis; long-term management relies on strict avoidance of fasting with an emergency illness regimen
Confirmation is by OXCT1 molecular testing or enzyme assay in fibroblasts, as biochemical markers can be subtle
reference.pathophysiology: SCOT (succinyl-CoA:3-ketoacid CoA transferase) catalyses the rate-limiting first step of ketone-body utilisation in extrahepatic tissues, transferring coenzyme A from succinyl-CoA to acetoacetate to form acetoacetyl-CoA. When the enzyme is deficient, peripheral tissues cannot use ketone bodies for energy, so ketones accumulate and are not cleared even when glucose is available. This produces persistent ketosis and a tendency to severe, life-threatening ketoacidosis during any period of increased ketogenesis, such as fasting or intercurrent illness. Because only ketone bodies accumulate, the organic acid and acylcarnitine profiles lack the specific markers seen in the isoleucine-pathway ketolysis defect.
additionalDifferentials: Ketotic hypoglycaemia and glycogen storage disorders
additionalInvestigations: Blood and urine ketone quantification demonstrating persistent ketosis in the fed state
Blood gas, glucose, electrolytes and anion gap during acute crises
Urine organic acids showing marked ketonuria without abnormal isoleucine metabolites
Plasma acylcarnitine profile (often normal, helping distinguish from other defects)
OXCT1 molecular genetic testing to confirm the diagnosis
SCOT enzyme activity assay in cultured fibroblasts where genetics are inconclusive
redFlags: Neonatal or infant presentation with severe high-anion-gap ketoacidosis
Persistent ketosis that does not resolve with feeding
Rapid deterioration with obtundation or cardiorespiratory compromise during a crisis
reference.prognosis: With prompt recognition and rigorous avoidance of fasting, many individuals do well and crises become less frequent with age, but early or severe ketoacidotic episodes can be fatal or cause neurological injury before diagnosis.
pitfalls: Overlooking the diagnosis because newborn screening and acylcarnitine profiles are typically normal
Interpreting persistent ketosis as dietary or presuming diabetes rather than a ketolysis defect
Allowing prolonged fasting for procedures without a protective glucose regimen
Assuming normal interictal biochemistry excludes the disorder when persistent low-grade ketosis is actually a clue
references: Scriver's OMMBID: Disorders of Ketone Body Metabolism
Saudubray, Baumgartner & Walter, Inborn Metabolic Diseases: Diagnosis and Treatment
management: Treat acute ketoacidotic crises with intravenous glucose to switch off ketogenesis and reverse catabolism, correcting acidosis and electrolyte disturbance
Prevent crises by strictly avoiding fasting, ensuring regular carbohydrate-containing feeds and frequent meals
Institute an emergency illness regimen with additional oral or intravenous glucose during intercurrent illness or reduced intake
Monitor blood and urine ketones, blood gases and anion gap, particularly during illness
Provide a written emergency management plan and educate the family to seek early treatment when unwell
Offer genetic counselling and family testing for autosomal recessive OXCT1 variants
Coordinate care through a specialist metabolic medicine team
